trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise). Clock starts at discovery: the first day the breach is known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member (164.404(a)(2))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ (the CAD database holds several years of patients)

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay as specified in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A business associate (MSP, ePCR, billing, CAD vendor) discovers a breach of the company's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (BAAs may set shorter)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information) of Florida residents. Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (15 more days if good cause is given to the department in writing within the 30 days, per 501.171(3)(a)); notice under the rules of the primary or functional federal regulator (HIPAA) is deemed compliant if the company timely provides a copy of that notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm the deemed-compliance path with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
A vendor that maintains the company's personal information has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination

trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida (interfacility trips to neighboring states are rare)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law

trigger: CAD or dispatch center outage affecting the county 911 zone
deadline: Immediately by phone to the county PSAP supervisor; written follow-up as the agreement requires
notify: County PSAP supervisor; county EMS contract manager

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
Per policy (typically as soon as practicable; use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment

deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Organizational incident handlers; CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official; FBI CJIS ISO

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)

deadline: As soon as practicable (voluntary; supports the OFAC mitigating factor)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
